anlamlar.tr: bir (belirsiz tanımlık; sessiz harfle başlayan kelimeden önce)
anlamlar.en: used before a singular noun that has not been mentioned before, when the next word begins with a consonant sound
ornekler: I have a brother and a sister.

anlamlar.en: used to mean "each" or "every" when talking about prices, speeds or how often
ornekler: I go to the gym three times a week.

anlamlar.tr: bir (belirsiz tanımlık; sesli harfle başlayan kelimeden önce)
anlamlar.en: used instead of "a" when the next word begins with a vowel sound
ornekler: It takes an hour to get there.

anlamlar.tr: (belirli tanımlık; bilinen, daha önce sözü geçen ya da tek olan şey için)
anlamlar.en: used before a noun when it is clear which person or thing you mean
ornekler: The sun is very hot today.

anlamlar.tr: (bir türün tamamı, enstrüman, ırmak, okyanus vb. adlardan önce)
anlamlar.en: used before some names and to talk about a whole group or type
ornekler: The Nile is the longest river in Africa.

anlamlar.en: used with two comparative forms to show that two things change together
ornekler: The more you practice, the better you get.

anlamlar.en: used by the speaker to refer to himself or herself as the subject of a verb
used to refer to the person or people you are speaking to
used to refer to people in general
ornekler: You never know what will happen.

anlamlar.en: used to refer to a man, boy or male animal as the subject of a verb
used to refer to a woman, girl or female animal as the subject of a verb
used to refer to a thing, animal or situation that has already been mentioned
ornekler: I bought a new phone. It's very fast.
Where's the cat? Is it outside?

anlamlar.en: used as the subject of a verb when talking about the weather, time, distance or a situation
used by the speaker to refer to himself or herself and one or more other people as the subject of a verb
used to refer to two or more people or things as the subject of a verb
ornekler: Where are my keys? Are they in the car?

anlamlar.tr: o (cinsiyeti bilinmeyen ya da belirtilmeyen tek kişi)
anlamlar.en: used to refer to one person when you do not know or do not want to say if it is a man or a woman
ornekler: Someone called, but they didn't leave a message.
Ask each student if they have a pen.

anlamlar.en: used to refer to people in general or people in authority
ornekler: They say it will rain tomorrow.

anlamlar.en: used as the object of a verb or preposition, or after "be", to refer to the speaker
used as the object of a verb or preposition to refer to a man, boy or male animal
used as the object of a verb or preposition to refer to a woman, girl or female animal
used as the object of a verb or preposition to refer to the speaker and another person or other people
used as the object of a verb or preposition to refer to two or more people or things
ornekler: I love these shoes. I'll buy them.

anlamlar.en: used to refer to one person when you do not know or do not want to say if it is a man or a woman
ornekler: If anyone calls, tell them I'm busy.
Every student should bring their book with them.

anlamlar.en: used to refer to something that belongs to the speaker
ornekler: Is that your car or mine?

anlamlar.en: used to refer to something that belongs to the person or people you are speaking to
ornekler: Our house is smaller than yours.

anlamlar.en: used to refer to something that belongs to a man, boy or male animal
ornekler: My phone is old, but his is new.

anlamlar.en: used to refer to something that belongs to a woman, girl or female animal
ornekler: Is this coat yours or hers?

anlamlar.en: used to refer to something that belongs to the speaker and another person or other people
ornekler: Their garden is bigger than ours.

anlamlar.en: used to refer to something that belongs to two or more people or things
ornekler: Our kids are older than theirs.

anlamlar.en: used as the object of a verb or preposition when the speaker is both the subject and the object
ornekler: I bought myself a new watch.

anlamlar.en: used to emphasize "I", or to mean "alone, without help"
ornekler: I did it all by myself.

anlamlar.en: used as the object of a verb or preposition when the person you are talking to is both the subject and the object
used to emphasize "you", or to mean "alone, without help"
ornekler: You can't do it all by yourself.

anlamlar.en: used as the object of a verb or preposition when a man or boy is both the subject and the object
ornekler: He looked at himself in the mirror.
He taught himself to play the guitar.

anlamlar.en: used to emphasize a male subject, or to mean "alone, without help"
ornekler: The president himself came to the opening.

anlamlar.en: used as the object of a verb or preposition when a woman or girl is both the subject and the object
ornekler: She bought herself a new dress.

anlamlar.en: used to emphasize a female subject, or to mean "alone, without help"
ornekler: She traveled around Asia by herself.

anlamlar.en: used as the object of a verb or preposition when a thing or animal is both the subject and the object
used to emphasize a thing or animal
ornekler: The town itself is very small.

anlamlar.en: used as the object of a verb or preposition when the speaker and others are both the subject and the object
ornekler: We enjoyed ourselves at the party.
We should be proud of ourselves.

anlamlar.en: used to emphasize "we", or to mean "alone, without help"
used as the object of a verb or preposition when the people you are talking to are both the subject and the object
used to emphasize "you" (plural), or to mean "alone, without help"
ornekler: You'll have to do it by yourselves.

anlamlar.en: used as the object of a verb or preposition when people or things are both the subject and the object
used to emphasize "they", or to mean "alone, without help"
ornekler: The students organized the event themselves.

anlamlar.en: used to refer to a person or thing that is near you, or to the present situation

anlamlar.tr: şu, o (uzaktaki şey ya da kişi; söylenen şey)
anlamlar.en: used to refer to a person or thing that is not near you, or to something already mentioned
used to introduce a part of a sentence that gives more information about a noun
ornekler: This is the book that I told you about.
The man that lives next door is a doctor.

anlamlar.en: used to refer to people or things that are near you
used to refer to people or things that are not near you
ornekler: Those are my parents over there.

anlamlar.en: used to mean "the people who" or "the things which"
ornekler: Those who finished early can go home.
The best seats are those at the front.

anlamlar.tr: (daha önce söz edilen şeyin yerine) olan, -i
anlamlar.en: used instead of a noun that has already been mentioned
ornekler: I don't like the blue shirt. I'll take the red one.

anlamlar.en: used to mean people in general, including the speaker (formal)
not one of a group of people or things, or not any of an amount
ornekler: "Is there any milk?" "No, there's none left."

anlamlar.en: used in questions and negatives to mean "any person"
any person, when it does not matter who
every person
every person

anlamlar.tr: (soru ve olumsuzda) bir şey, hiçbir şey
anlamlar.en: used in questions and negatives to mean "a thing"
any thing, when it does not matter which
ornekler: You can eat anything you like.

anlamlar.en: all things, or all the things in a group
no person
not anything
ornekler: I have nothing to do today.

anlamlar.en: used to ask for information about something
the thing or things that
ornekler: I don't understand what you mean.

anlamlar.en: used to ask about one or more things from a limited group
ornekler: Which of these do you like?

anlamlar.en: used to introduce extra information about a thing
ornekler: The house, which is very old, is for sale.
This is the bus which goes to the airport.

anlamlar.en: used to ask about the name or identity of a person
used to introduce information about a person
ornekler: The woman who lives here is a doctor.
I have a friend who speaks five languages.

anlamlar.en: used instead of "who" as the object of a verb or preposition (formal)
ornekler: To whom should I send the letter?
The man whom I met was very kind.

anlamlar.en: used to ask who something belongs to
used to show who or what something belongs to
ornekler: That's the girl whose father is a pilot.
I met a man whose car was stolen.

anlamlar.en: any person who, or the person who
ornekler: Whoever wins will get a prize.
Whoever told you that was wrong.

anlamlar.en: used to show that each person in a group does something to the others
ornekler: We help each other with homework.
